content: This medication, commonly known as Pepto-Bismol or Pink Bismuth, is used to treat occasional upset stomach, heartburn, nausea, diarrhea, and to help prevent travelers' diarrhea. It works by slowing the growth of bacteria that may be causing diarrhea. However, it should not be used to self-treat diarrhea if you also have a fever or blood/mucus in your stools, as these could indicate a more serious condition. Additionally, this medication may be prescribed by a doctor in combination with other medications to treat stomach ulcers caused by Helicobacter pylori bacteria. It is not recommended to self-treat ulcers with this product. Bismuth subsalicylate is a salicylate, and it is important to check the product label for ingredients, even if you have used it before, as manufacturers may change formulations. Products with similar names may contain different ingredients intended for other purposes. To use this medication, take it orally as needed, following the instructions on the product packaging or as directed by your doctor. The dosage depends on your age, medical condition, and response to treatment. Do not increase the dose or take it more frequently than directed. If using chewable tablets, chew them thoroughly before swallowing. This medication may interact with other drugs, such as tetracycline antibiotics or chloroquine, potentially reducing their absorption. If your doctor has instructed you to use this medication daily, take it regularly to achieve the best results. Inform your doctor if your condition persists or worsens. Common side effects include darkening of the stools or tongue, which are generally harmless. Serious side effects, such as persistent vomiting or diarrhea leading to dehydration, or rare but severe stomach or intestinal bleeding, may occur. Allergic reactions to this medication are rare but can be serious. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, aspirin, salicylates (e.g., salsalate), NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen, celecoxib), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Some formulations may also contain aspartame. Children and teenagers under 18 should not use this product if they have chickenpox, flu, or any undiagnosed illness, or if they have recently received a vaccine, due to the risk of Reye's syndrome. Pregnant individuals should consult their doctor before use, as this medication may harm an unborn baby and cause complications during labor or delivery. It is not recommended for use during pregnancy from 20 weeks until delivery. If deemed necessary between 20 and 30 weeks of pregnancy, the lowest effective dose should be used for the shortest possible time. This medication should not be used after 30 weeks of pregnancy. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, but similar drugs do and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may increase the risk of bleeding when taken with other drugs that also cause bleeding. Carefully check the labels of all prescription and non-prescription medications, as many contain pain relievers or fever reducers (NSAIDs such as aspirin, ibuprofen, or naproxen) that are similar to this drug and may increase the risk of side effects. If your doctor has instructed you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81-162 milligrams per day), continue taking the aspirin unless otherwise directed. This medication may interfere with certain medical or laboratory tests, such as X-rays of the intestines using contrast dye, potentially causing false test results. Inform your healthcare provider or lab personnel if you are using this medication. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you are taking this medication for diarrhea, drink plenty of water to reduce the risk of dehydration. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it or store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
